narrationScript: The rise of Artificial Intelligence introduces even more complex ethical dilemmas. As AI systems become more autonomous, questions of accountability become paramount. Who is responsible when a self-driving car makes an error, or a medical AI misdiagnoses? This leads us to Explainable AI, or XAI, which aims to make AI decisions understandable to humans, moving beyond opaque 'black boxes.' Beyond accountability, AI also poses risks for surveillance, manipulation, and the creation of deepfakes that spread misinformation. But our ethical considerations extend beyond AI to the broader societal impact of technology. The digital divide, for instance, highlights unequal access to technology, exacerbating existing inequalities. As developers, we must ensure our creations are accessible to everyone, regardless of their socioeconomic status or physical abilities. Similarly, the spread of misinformation through social media shows how powerful tools can be weaponized. We have a role in designing systems that promote truth and critical thinking, not just engagement.
